title: Mud tower houses anchor village life in Koutammakou
body: In the Togo-Benin border region, Batammariba communities build earthen tower houses called takienta. The houses form part of villages that include places for ceremonies, springs and sacred sites.
takeaway: A village's layout can show how dwelling, farming and ceremony fit together in everyday life.
visual: an earthen tower house beside a small cluster of cylindrical granaries

title: Mining brought workers from three countries into Chile's desert towns
body: At the Humberstone and Santa Laura saltpetre works, workers from Chile, Peru and Bolivia lived in company settlements. Beginning in the late 19th century, they developed a common culture known as pampino.
takeaway: A shared workplace and a remote setting can bring people with different origins into the same community.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works (2005)
visual: small workers' homes lining a dusty street in the Atacama

title: US intermarriage rose from about 3% to 17% of newlyweds
body: Pew Research Center compared newly married Americans across racial and ethnic categories. It found that around 17% of people who married in 2015 had a spouse of a different race or ethnicity, up from about 3% in 1967.
takeaway: New marriages show changing patterns sooner than a count of all couples, which includes people who married decades earlier.
source: Pew Research Center, Intermarriage in the U.S. 50 Years After Loving v. Virginia (2017)
visual: a small wedding gathering under trees seen from a distance

title: In July 2020, most US adults aged 18 to 29 lived with a parent
body: A Pew analysis of US survey data found 52% of adults aged 18 to 29 lived with one or both parents in July 2020, up from 47% that February. The rise came during the first months of the COVID-19 pandemic.
takeaway: Households can change quickly when work, education and housing arrangements change at once.
source: Pew Research Center, A Majority of Young Adults in the U.S. Live With Their Parents (2020)
visual: a young adult carrying a suitcase through the doorway of a family home
